messages.message:
Patch Set 3:

(10 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Experimental feature testing in progress, please pay attention to the comments

Some concerns, see inline comments. The macro additions themselves read well, but three of the conversions change behaviour rather than just tidying it: the lds_def_comp_size_cnt rework computes the wrong capacity, OBD_ALLOC_PTR_ARRAY_LARGE() silently drops the vmalloc fallback on the pre-5.15 kernels still listed in lustre/ChangeLog, and osp_sync.c keeps using arr_size as a byte count after it became an element count. It may be worth splitting the lod_def_striping_comp_resize() semantic change and the osp_sync.c cookie-array rework out from the mechanical OBD_ALLOC()->OBD_ALLOC_PTR_ARRAY() conversions, since the latter are easy to review in bulk and the former are not.

commit.subject: LU-6142 obdclass: add/use OBD_ALLOC_PTR_ARRAY[_LARGE]()
commit.message:
LU-6142 obdclass: add/use OBD_ALLOC_PTR_ARRAY[_LARGE]()

Add new allocation macros OBD_ALLOC_PTR_ARRAY() and
OBD_ALLOC_PTR_ARRAY_LARGE() to allocate struct arrays
instead of open-coding array sizes, and instead use the
kernel k[v]malloc_array() functions.  Also add matching
OBD_FREE_PTR_ARRAY() and OBD_FREE_PTR_ARRAY_LARGE()
counterparts.  These simplify callers and avoids potential
bugs with overflow of calculations with 32-bit variables.

Convert OBD_ALLOC() and OBD_ALLOC_LARGE() and corresponding
OBD_FREE[_LARGE]() callers to the new macros where possible.

Change lds_def_comp_size_cnt to hold the maximum count of
entries in the lds_def_comp_entries array, rather than the
requested number of entries.  This avoids recalculating
the array size on each call so lod_free_def_comp_buffer()
and lod_free_comp_buffers() can use OBD_FREE_PTR_ARRAY().

Cleanup code style issues in related code.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Dilger <adilger@thelustrecollective.com>
Change-Id: Ie0db250d017d228606d4d976132968d138500c1e
